Hollywood, they say, is dying. But at my local Starbucks in LA, the creative culture of Tinseltown is very much alive.

LA seems to have developed a peculiar enthusiasm for writing its own obituary. Studios are cutting spending. Film production is migrating elsewhere.

But I’m still holding out hope for Hollywood, even as jobs disappear. Because the entertainment industry and the creative culture that sustains it are not the same thing, and the latter is very much alive.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

I meet the people at the heart of Hollywood every time I go to my local Starbucks on McCadden Place and Hollywood Boulevard.

The most familiar face at the register is one of those cheerful twenty-three-year-olds whose untainted happiness makes you feel both ancient and vaguely protective of him.

He has a more seasoned colleague who says he is “thirty, but emotionally forty.”

I didn’t learn he was an actor until I asked how he was doing, and he said he felt like he just fell off a horse.

“Don’t we all,” I replied.

“No, literally,” he said. “I fell off a horse yesterday.”

He was learning to ride for a film role, he explained. And with that fact, he opened up his green apron.

The Actor — as I began to call him — is also taking clowning classes, although he specified “not the big red nose kind.” Think Buster Keaton-style clowning in the vein of performance art. The guy drizzling caramel syrup at 8:00 a.m. is an immersive theater actor.

And as for my beaming barista at the register — well, it turns out that he makes short films.

The Filmmaker is shooting a film and has another in post-production. He enjoys making films about musicians.

He works the register, sending orders to the Actor for candy-colored atrocities that seem to have forgotten their coffee ancestry. But theirs is more than a barista bond.

The Filmmaker recently helped the Actor staff a feature film project. He is also planning a music video with two other musician baristas.

That this constellation of quirky entertainers came to exist under the roof of one soulless corporate coffee chain can only lead me to one conclusion.

It is one that I realize will be unpopular and deeply uncool, so let me preface it by saying I’ve lived here nine years. Long enough to have witnessed a calamity or two.

This is still a fantastic town.

It’s not that the decline of the entertainment industry is imaginary. For most of the twentieth century, filmmakers had little choice but to come to LA for the big studios and jobs.

Beginning in the 1990s, Hollywood began losing productions to cities offering lower costs and generous tax incentives.

LA no longer has a monopoly on the cinematic universe.

But something survived the industry’s decentralization: the concentration of people who want to make things.

My baristas aren’t waiting for Hollywood to give them jobs. They’re making films and recruiting one another for projects, all while wearing identical green aprons.

Last week, Swift attended the Chiefs’ 22-6 win over the Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium, and took in the action from a suite with her family and friends.

The “Cleveland” singer was shown on the CBS broadcast alongside her mother-in-law, Donna Kelce, Fever star Caitlin Clark and singer Este Haim cheering for the Chiefs tight end after he completed a catch over the middle in the second quarter.

Swift and Clark, who is a Chiefs fan and a friend of Kelce, previously watched the Chiefs take on the Texans in a suite at Arrowhead Stadium in January 2025.

Taylor Swift loves what she is seeing. pic.twitter.com/vxEhz65591

Clark had a pop-up Nike at the “New Heights” podcast tailgate last Sunday. Travis and his brother, retired Super Bowl champion center-turned ESPN analyst Jason Kelce, host the show together.

Swift attended the Week 6 clash after she performed at the Academy Museum Gala the night before in Los Angeles.

The 14-time Grammy winner jets around in her private plane — which made headlines when she flew from Tokyo to Los Angeles, and then Las Vegas to watch the Chiefs defeat the 49ers in overtime in Super Bowl 2024.

Swift and Kelce were married on July 3 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, nearly a year after getting engaged.

Luka Doncic is already putting his stamp in the Lakers’ history books.

He had 52 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists in the Lakers’ 132-123 win over the Jazz on Sunday, surpassing LeBron James for sixth-most 40-point games with the Lakers.

James was with the Lakers for eight seasons, his longest consecutive stretch anywhere in his career. Doncic, whom the Lakers acquired in a trade from the Mavericks in February 2025, is entering this third season in Los Angeles.

It was the 10th time in Doncic’s career that he has scored 50 or more points. Since Doncic entered the league as the third overall pick by the Mavericks in 2018, only James Harden (16) and Damian Lillard (11) have had more 50-point performances than Doncic.

Doncic helped the Lakers storm back from an 18-point first-quarter deficit against the Jazz to jump to 3-0 record.

Doncic recently told the California Post that he hopes to spend the rest of his career with the Lakers.

“Hopefully, yeah,” Dončić told the California Post. “But as you know in this NBA business, you never know what’s going to happen. But I feel like I’ve found something here that’s very comfortable for me. And hopefully [that happens].”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Voter ID is the only way to fix California’s broken election system.

That’s the only reasonable conclusion from Sunday’s extraordinary hearing at the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.

A three-judge panel heard the Trump administration’s case against non-citizen voting in California.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Earlier this month, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) gave California a thumb drive with 20,000 names on it, ostensibly containing the names of suspected non-citizens who had registered to vote in the state.

State and county officials, who had already sent ballots out by mail, refused to open it.

So the DOJ sued in district court, hoping to force California to set aside those 20,000 ballots if and when they came in.

Time is of the essence: ballots are already being mailed back, and counted. And once they are in, it’s almost impossible to fish them out again.

The district judge set a hearing date eight days after the case was filed. Normally, that’s quick. But in the middle of a vote-by-mail election, it meant that hundreds of thousands of ballots would be counted in the interim.

So the Trump administration appealed to the Ninth Circuit to intervene.

The judges — two Trump appointees, one Biden appointee — seemed skeptical of the DOJ’s case, at first.

After all, the Constitution’s Elections Clause leaves it to the states to decide how to run their election.

Sure, federal law prohibits non-citizens from voting — as does state law in California — but normally it’s up to California to figure out how to enforce that.

And if California decides not to make voters prove they are citizens — if it just asks them to “attest” that they are — that might be lame, but it might also be within California’s right to do so.

The Tenth Amendment — important to conservatives — also prevents the federal government from forcing the states to enforce federal laws.

That’s called “commandeering” — and Trump can’t force California to enforce federal laws against non-citizens voting. Nor can Trump make the state enforce its own laws, either.

The judges — including the Trump appointees — were also worried about stepping into the lower court case too soon.

Why the rush? And if the federal government was concerned about votes being counted before non-citizen ballots could be separated, why hadn’t it acted sooner?

The DOJ, represented by Matthew Donnelly, said that the administration didn’t have a reliable list of non-citizen voters until recently.

Whether the judges buy that explanation remains to be seen.

But the judges also had one lingering question for the State of California’s lawyers that they could not answer.

If it’s illegal for non-citizens to vote in California, how does the state stop them from voting?

California’s lawyers seemed to have no answer.

“Your Honor, I honestly don’t know the answer to that.”

The state seemed to argue that anyone could challenge a non-citizen’s ballot as it was being cast.

(How are you supposed to do that — hide in a mailbox?)

Suppose someone does challenge a ballot. The judges asked how the state would verify the accusation.

“There could very well be a verification process,” a lawyer for the state replied.

Could be? You mean, they don’t know?

Well, he said, he was sure that a losing candidate could bring some kind of challenge. But he’d have to have overwhelming evidence, and there would have to be enough non-citizen votes to make the difference in the election.

Good luck finding that evidence after an election. Especially when California takes several weeks to count the votes.

Here’s where things stand.

California bars non-citizens from voting. But it doesn’t require anyone to prove citizenship when they register.

If a non-citizen casts a ballot, there’s almost no practical way to challenge it.

The State of California set the system up this way — on purpose.

They say that very few non-citizens vote — but they make it impossible to know.

And they’re proud of it. Smug, even. What are you going to do about it?

Well, there is one thing to do about it.

There’s Proposition 39, which would require voters to have valid ID to vote.

It’s the only way to make sure that only citizens vote in California’s elections.

It’s curious that Democrats are so determined to stop it.

Joel Pollak is Opinion editor of The California Post.

news.originalContent:
Storms Boelo and Austen kill a man in Scotland and cut power to thousands of homes in the UK, France and Germany.

A pair of storms battering northern Europe have killed one man, cut power to more than 150,000 homes, and disrupted flights and phone networks.

More than 82,000 homes in the United Kingdom, nearly 60,000 in France, and at least 10,000 in Germany had no electricity on Sunday after storms Boelo and Austen passed through the region within 24 hours, according to authorities in the countries.

A falling tree killed a man, 60, in southwestern Scotland on Sunday, while another falling tree injured two women in central Scotland, the Press Association reported.

Winds of up to 135 km/h (84 mph) were recorded in the Argyll and Bute regions of western Scotland. Trees and power cables brought down by the storm blocked roads and rail lines across Scotland and northern England.

In Brighton, on England’s southern coast, Austen blew away an unused pier on Friday.

Authorities have warned of flood risk in regions of both Scotland and England.

The Met Office, the UK’s national forecaster, warned that Boelo would bring a danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves and said people should stay indoors as much as possible.

Across the English Channel, Europe battled its first big storm of the autumn, with strong winds inflicting widespread power cuts.

French energy company Enedis said that at Austen’s peak on Saturday, some 288,000 homes had no electricity. Some 59,000 remained without power at midday Sunday, mainly in Normandy and Brittany.

A marathon runner in the midst of a race in northern France was lightly injured by a tree knocked over in strong winds.

In Germany, Austen cut power to 10,000 homes in and around the southwestern town of Freiburg-Breisgau on Sunday. The town’s main hospital said it had to limit service to emergency cases because of the blackout, which also cut the mobile phone network.

German police said two people were seriously hurt on Saturday by scaffolding blown away by Austen’s strong winds at a market in the town of Nastatten.

The storms also hit the Netherlands and Belgium, where falling trees injured four people in Brussels on Saturday.

In the Netherlands, north of the island of Schiermonnikoog, three crew members on board a freight ship were injured in the storms, according to the country’s coastguard. Two of them were winched off and taken by helicopter to a hospital on the mainland.

The storms caused hundreds of flights to be cancelled or diverted across northern Europe, including at Amsterdam’s Schiphol airport, one of the continent’s busiest hubs.

Experts have warned of more extreme weather events due to climate change.

In the Netherlands, north of the island of Schiermonnikoog, three crew members on board a freight ship were injured in the storms, according to the country’s coastguard. Two of them were winched off and taken by helicopter to a hospital on the mainland.

The storms caused hundreds of flights to be cancelled or diverted across northern Europe, including at Amsterdam’s Schiphol airport, one of the continent’s busiest hubs.

Experts have warned of more extreme weather events due to climate change.

news.originalContent:
Leftist president mounts stunning comeback after unexpected first-round loss galvanised supporters of Flavio Bolsonaro.

Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s contentious presidential race, pulling off a remarkable comeback after a first-round loss that galvanised the country’s political right.

Shortly after 9pm Brasilia time on Sunday (00:00 GMT), Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court called the race for Lula, who had earned more than 51 percent of the vote. More than 64 million ballots were cast for the incumbent.

Bolsonaro, meanwhile, netted 48 percent, or north of 59 million ballots. More than 4 million votes separated the two candidates, with the final votes still being counted.

Coughing and audibly hoarse, Lula took to a flag-draped podium shortly after to give his victory speech. He acknowledged clashes ahead, including with his legislative agenda.

“I do not choose the Congress,” he said. “It was the people who chose it, and it is with them that I will vote, work and get things approved.”

He also thanked the voters who cast their ballots “to secure democracy in the country”.

With his victory, Lula has made history. No other politician in modern Brazilian history has lost the first round of a presidential election only to win the second.

“A historic turning point for democracy,” Edinho Silva, the head of Lula’s Workers’ Party, posted on social media, along with a video of supporters chanting, “Ole, ole, ole, ole, ola! Lula, Lula!”

But Bolsonaro has so far refused to concede, teeing up a likely court battle over the legality of a Supreme Court decision to extend the voting time by two hours.

“It is impossible to acknowledge the result,” Bolsonaro said in a short speech, accusing the Supreme Court of having “changed the rules of the game mid-game”. He added that he would seek an annulment of the results.

Leaders across the Western Hemisphere, particularly on the left, applauded the result. “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil have won,” Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum wrote in the wake of the results. “Congratulations, President Lula!”

United States Senator Bernie Sanders likewise offered his felicitations, calling Lula’s re-election “extraordinary”.

“Lula has stood up for Brazilian workers & democracy — and will continue to do so in the next four years,” Sanders said in a statement.

Still, the vote process was marred by allegations of voter suppression after reports emerged that public transport in some areas had been suspended.

Lula’s allies accused Bolsonaro’s supporters of reducing bus availability in an attempt to dampen the president’s working-class base.

Heavy rains, meanwhile, affected southern areas considered to be Bolsonaro strongholds.

The campaigns of both Lula and Bolsonaro ultimately petitioned the Supreme Court for a voting extension. Polls across the country were kept open two hours later than expected, until 7pm Brasilia time (22:00 GMT), following a ruling from Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin.

Bolsonaro, however, has argued that some polling stations were not able to reopen in time, harming any additional votes he may have earned.

Sunday’s victory means Lula will retain the presidency of Latin America’s largest country, denying a crucial victory to the region’s right wing.

In recent years, right-wing leaders have swept presidential races in nearby countries like Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Bolivia and Ecuador. Many have ridden a wave of anti-incumbent energy and enjoyed support from US President Donald Trump, who returned to office in January 2025.

A former union leader for metalworkers, Lula – at age 80 – will be sworn in on January 5, 2027, when he will beat his own record as the oldest Brazilian president to take the oath of office since the country’s return to democracy.

His victory has earned him an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term.

Lula came into Sunday’s run-off as an underdog. While he narrowly led pre-election, the first round of voting on October 4 showed him trailing Bolsonaro.

He earned 45 percent of the first-round vote, compared with the right-wing senator’s 47 percent, both tallies short of the 50 percent needed to avoid a run-off.

But in the weeks since, Lula has rallied supporters around cost-of-living issues. He championed a constitutional amendment passed this month that shortened the Brazilian workweek, and floated the possibility of providing free public transport on weekends.

Having entered politics in the 1980s, during the twilight of the country’s military dictatorship, Lula has run for president seven times.

He won two consecutive terms from 2002 through 2010, as well as a third term in 2022, in what was the tightest race in modern Brazilian history up to that point.

His rival in that election, former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, is the father of Senator Bolsonaro, Lula’s adversary in this race.

Jair Bolsonaro has since been sentenced to 27 years in prison for his role in plotting a coup following his loss to Lula.

Despite overseeing a decline in poverty and low unemployment during his third term, Lula has faced questions about his advanced age, his ability to combat crime, and the country’s polarised political landscape.

An explosion of household debt has also left many Brazilians feeling their economic circumstances have worsened.

In September, Lula banned online gambling and sport betting apps to address the issue.

While the victory over Bolsonaro cements Lula’s status as one of the most significant and influential figures in Brazil’s modern history, efforts to advance legislative priorities during his fourth term could be stymied by the most right-wing Congress in recent memory.

There are also questions about how Bolsonaro’s right-wing base and the Trump administration might react to Lula’s re-election.

Already, Bolsonaro has suggested he would seek to nullify the election, citing the prolonged voting hours.

“What happened today was not normal. It was, in fact, unacceptable,” Bolsonaro told his supporters.

Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, also suggested there had been judicial malpractice as a result of the extension.

“If a conservative government in Brazil did this, everyone in the mainstream press in America would lose their minds, but I guess they’re just choosing to be silent because it’s all for the cause,” Trump Jr wrote on social media.

The Trump White House has been openly supportive of the Bolsonaro family, issuing 50-percent tariffs last year on certain Brazilian products in a push to end the prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro.

Judges involved in the case were also subjected to US sanctions, most notably Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

Lula has framed such manoeuvres as an attack on the sovereignty of Brazil’s judicial system.

One of Trump’s critics, US Representative Ro Khanna, suggested the US president could take further actions against Brazil in response to Sunday’s vote.

“People all across the world are fighting back against extremism. With Lula in Brazil, they just won,” Khanna wrote.

“Trump must respect the results and not undermine Brazil’s elections.”

news.originalContent:
بی‌بی‌سی دریافته است که مگان مارکل، همسر شاهزاده هری پسر دوم پادشاه بریتانیا، پارسال ارتباط با پدرش را قطع کرد و به او گفت که خودش و مقامات می‌دانند که او دختران خردسال را آزار داده است.

منابع نزدیک به مگان مارکل می‌گویند که او در نامه‌ای به پدرش، توماس مارکل، هشدار داد که دیگر نوه‌هایش را نخواهد دید.

گفته می‌شود که این نامه زمانی برای توماس مارکل، ۸۲ ساله، ارسال شد که پس از جراحی قطع پا در بیمارستانی در فیلیپین بستری بود.

براساس گزارش‌ها، تصاویری از سوءاستفاده جنسی از کودکان، که گفته می‌شود متعلق به توماس مارکل است، در خانه سابق او در فیلیپین پیدا شده است.

پلیس بریتانیا هم در سال ۲۰۱۹ مگان مارکل را در جریان اتهام‌های وارده به پدرش قرار داده بود. توماس مارکل که اکنون در ایالات متحده ساکن است، تمامی این اتهام‌ها را رد می‌کند.

مگان مارکل از سال ۲۰۱۸ با پدرش قطع رابطه کرده است. در آن سال، پدرش برای مشکل سلامتی در مراسم عروسی سلطنتی دخترش شرکت نکرد.

به نظر می‌رسد نامه‌ای که مگان مارکل در سال ۲۰۲۵ برای پدرش فرستاد، نقطه پایانی بر رابطه پرچالش این پدر و دختر بوده است.

این نامه نخست در گزارش امروز یکشنبه روزنامه بریتانیایی سان منتشر شد. بنابر این گزارش مگان مارکل به پدرش نوشته است که دگر نوه‌هایش، آرچی و لیلی‌بت، را نخواهد دید و خودش هم هیچ‌وقت با او تماس نخواهد گرفت.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

توماس مارکل جونیور، برادر ناتنی مگان، روز جمعه به روزنامه سان گفت که مجموعه‌ای از عکس و ویدئو پدرش را در خانه سابق او در فیلیپین پیدا کرده است.

گفته می‌شود او در ماه ژوئیه به اف‌بی‌آی اطلاع داد که در میان آنها ویدیوها و تصاویری مربوط به سوءاستفاده از کودکان یافته است.

اف‌بی‌آی تایید کرده است که از این اتهامات آگاه است.

مارکل جونیور ۶۰ ساله، در مصاحبه‌اش با روزنامه سان از مگان عذرخواهی کرد چرا که در دوران طولانی قطع رابطه ابتدا جانب پدرش را گرفته بود.

او گفت: «اکنون می‌دانم که در ۹ سال گذشته، از فرد اشتباه حمایت می‌کرده‌ام.»

مقامات فیلیپین تایید کرده‌اند که در حال بررسی اتهام‌های پدر مگان مارکل هستند. آنها روز جمعه به بی‌بی‌سی گفتند که کارگروه مبارزه با قاچاق انسان و بهره‌کشی جنسی از کودکان مشغول رسیدگی به این موضوع است.

جان‌ویک رمولا، وزیر کشور فیلیپین، نیز اعلام کرد که پلیس کامپیوتر توماس مارکل را ضبط کرده است و قرار است بررسی‌های دقیق ویژه جرایم جنایی انجام دهد.

در همین حال، توماس مارکل در مصاحبه‌ای با روزنامه میل آن ساندی اذعان کرد که در سفرهای پیشین خود به فیلیپین در ازای رابطه جنسی پول پرداخت کرده است اما رابطه جنسی با دختران زیر سن قانونی و داشتن تصاویر مربوط به سوءاستفاده جنسی از کودکان را تکذیب کرد.

این تحولات در حالی رخ می‌دهد که پلیس متروپولیتن لندن روز شنبه (۲۴ اکتبر) تایید کرد که در سال ۲۰۱۹ نامه‌ای حاوی «چندین ادعا» در مورد پدر مگان دریافت کرده بود.

منابع نزدیک به مگان مارکل می‌گویند که او در نامه‌ای به پدرش، توماس مارکل، هشدار داد که دیگر نوه‌هایش را نخواهد دید.

گفته می‌شود که این نامه زمانی برای توماس مارکل، ۸۲ ساله، ارسال شد که پس از جراحی قطع پا در بیمارستانی در فیلیپین بستری بود.

براساس گزارش‌ها، تصاویری از سوءاستفاده جنسی از کودکان، که گفته می‌شود متعلق به توماس مارکل است، در خانه سابق او در فیلیپین پیدا شده است.

پلیس بریتانیا هم در سال ۲۰۱۹ مگان مارکل را در جریان اتهام‌های وارده به پدرش قرار داده بود. توماس مارکل که اکنون در ایالات متحده ساکن است، تمامی این اتهام‌ها را رد می‌کند.

مگان مارکل از سال ۲۰۱۸ با پدرش قطع رابطه کرده است. در آن سال، پدرش برای مشکل سلامتی در مراسم عروسی سلطنتی دخترش شرکت نکرد.

به نظر می‌رسد نامه‌ای که مگان مارکل در سال ۲۰۲۵ برای پدرش فرستاد، نقطه پایانی بر رابطه پرچالش این پدر و دختر بوده است.

این نامه نخست در گزارش امروز یکشنبه روزنامه بریتانیایی سان منتشر شد. بنابر این گزارش مگان مارکل به پدرش نوشته است که دگر نوه‌هایش، آرچی و لیلی‌بت، را نخواهد دید و خودش هم هیچ‌وقت با او تماس نخواهد گرفت.

توماس مارکل جونیور، برادر ناتنی مگان، روز جمعه به روزنامه سان گفت که مجموعه‌ای از عکس و ویدئو پدرش را در خانه سابق او در فیلیپین پیدا کرده است.

گفته می‌شود او در ماه ژوئیه به اف‌بی‌آی اطلاع داد که در میان آنها ویدیوها و تصاویری مربوط به سوءاستفاده از کودکان یافته است.

اف‌بی‌آی تایید کرده است که از این اتهامات آگاه است.

مارکل جونیور ۶۰ ساله، در مصاحبه‌اش با روزنامه سان از مگان عذرخواهی کرد چرا که در دوران طولانی قطع رابطه ابتدا جانب پدرش را گرفته بود.

او گفت: «اکنون می‌دانم که در ۹ سال گذشته، از فرد اشتباه حمایت می‌کرده‌ام.»

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez’s big win against Meta last week means huge risks for every successful company in America; if this decision holds up, the same garbage-lawsuit model could destroy any business.

It’s a victory for speech policing, too.

A Sante Fe jury found Meta guilty of 43 million violations of state consumer-protection law by buying a whole series of absurd arguments, including:

That’s more than twice the state’s annual budget; Torrez is bragging that he has funded education for decades with this victory.

Mind you, New Mexico’s lawyers didn’t actually show that terrible content actually proliferated, nor that anyone anywhere was injured in any way by any of this.

All they could point to was a political consulting firm’s potential abuse of Facebook data to better target online ads in favor of Donald Trump in 2016, plus another similarly mild “data breach” — both of which the company later ensured wouldn’t happen again.

New Mexico’s insanely ambulance-chaser-friendly laws, plus its juries’ and courts’ strong inclination to award huge judgments, have rightly earned it a ranking as one of the nation’s worst “judicial hellholes.”

Plus, Torrez’s office didn’t even have to argue the case: It contracted the work out to private tort attorneys in exchange for a cut of the fines — over $10 billion if the decision holds up.

Oh, and: To appeal, Meta must post bond of 2½ times the judgment — over $60 billion.

The particular argument here was extremely odious, all but insisting that consumers can only be protected by some “anti-misinformation” — that is, Big Brother controls on speech.

Surprise, surprise: Torrez is one of the “Soros prosecutors,” initially elected thanks to funding from the lefty billionaire to quit fighting regular crime and instead pursue an extremist progressive agenda with lawfare instead of legislation.

But the bottom line is a threat to any business in America: You can be hauled into a New Mexico kangaroo court on some cockamamie theory, with zero evidence anyone ever suffered as a result, and fined more than the value of your entire company — and unable to appeal unless you can cough up even more cash to post bond.

Obviously, the threat is most dire to successful tech companies and other industries seen as villains in the strongly Democratic state: For them, New Mexico law is an even bigger menace than the European Union’s statutes, which at least limit the extent of (utterly unjust) fines.

Luckily for the rest of the US private sector, Meta has the resources and the will to fight back all the way to the US Supreme Court if necessary.

Pray the company triumphs completely, or New Mexico could wind up choking the entire US economy.

LAS VEGAS – The Rams saw a door crack open with the 49ers’ first loss of the season on Sunday and refused to let it slam shut. Sensing the crossroads they stood at, they thrashed the Raiders 35-21 with the urgency of a team unwilling to let an opportunity to climb back into the division race, and nudge their season back on track.

Rams played with desperation

The Rams arrived in Las Vegas wounded, desperate and running out of room for another disappointment.

With an energy and edge that reflected the urgency of their circumstances, the Rams took the Raiders to school in a first-half masterclass, building a 28-6 lead that felt every bit as decisive as it looked.

The Raiders showed some life in the second half, closing the lead to 28-18 in the fourth quarter, but the Rams responded with a 12-play, 70-yard touchdown drive to restore order and push the lead back to 35-18.

It all started with the dominant first half.

There was nothing complicated about the message.

One team understood how much was at stake and went about doing something about it. The other spent the half absorbing the lesson.

Matthew Stafford was the head instructor.

Turning back the clock, the veteran quarterback completed 17 of 19 passes for 148 yards and three touchdowns, taking command of the game with the precision and confidence of someone who had no intention of letting another opportunity slip away.

Two incompletions. Three touchdown passes.

That pretty much told the story.

Stafford finished 23 of 29 for 195 yards and 3 touchdowns.

The Raiders needed to make Stafford uncomfortable. Instead, they gave him a stage. And the longer the half went, the more it became clear that the Rams’ problems entering the afternoon were doing nothing to diminish their ability to create them for somebody else.

For all the attention paid to what was wrong with the Rajms, there was still a dangerous football team underneath the bruises.

The Raiders found that out the hard way.

There are plenty of ways to explain how an NFL game gets away from a team. Sometimes, though, the numbers handle the explanation themselves.

As was the case when the Rams built their big lead.

Rams: Four red-zone trips, four touchdowns.

Raiders: Three red-zone trips, zero touchdowns.

And there was your 28-6 Rams lead, a scoreboard that reflected the enormous difference between creating opportunities and actually doing something with them.

The Raiders got close enough to make this a game. They just never did enough once they got there.

The Rams, meanwhile, treated every trip inside the 20 like an obligation to finish. No letting the Raiders off the hook. No wasting the work that put them in scoring position. Just touchdowns, one after another, until a potentially competitive afternoon became an exercise in trying to escape a hole.

Pair that with the Rams getting the better of the turnover battle, and the Raiders were losing in the two areas most capable of making everything else irrelevant.

Nothing says ballgame quite like that combination.

You can move the ball between the 20s. You can find enough successful plays to convince yourself the offense is functioning. But when one team keeps cashing opportunities for seven points and the other keeps walking away without a touchdown, the math turns brutal in a hurry.

For the Raiders, that made this especially frustrating. Three red-zone possessions represented three chances to apply pressure, keep pace or at least give their defense some breathing room.

Instead, those opportunities became another reminder of how costly their finishing problems have become.

That is on top of the third-quarter gift the Raider got by way of a Kyren Williams fumble that set them up at in Rams territory.

Only for the drive to stall at the Rams 25.

Credit the Rams defense, which stood tall in their moments of truth.

They understood the assignment. A wounded team needing a win played with the urgency to seize its chances and the precision to maximize them.

The Raiders supplied the opposite.

And by the time the deficit reached 22 points, the difference between the teams required very little further explanation.

Rams carved up the Raiders weakness

There was no mystery about how Sean McVay and the Rams would attack the Raiders on Sunday.

Not with Las Vegas arriving at Allegiant Stadium sporting the NFL’s fifth-worst run defense. And certainly not with a Rams offense desperate to rediscover its physical identity and get its season back on track.

The blueprint was obvious. Pound the football, establish control at the line of scrimmage and force the Raiders to prove they could stop it.

The Rams hammered away for 199 rushing yards on 38 carries, averaging over five yards per attempt in a punishing display that exposed one of the Raiders’ biggest weaknesses.

It wasn’t necessarily complicated football. In fact, that was the beauty of it from the Rams’ perspective.

McVay identified a vulnerability, attacked it relentlessly and watched his offensive line impose its will on a Raiders defense that had few answers.

And the ramifications extended well beyond the rushing statistics.

By establishing the ground game, the Rams created favorable down-and-distance situations, kept the Raiders’ pass rush from teeing off on Matthew Stafford and opened opportunities for their passing attack.

It was complementary offensive football at its finest, with the running game serving as the foundation for everything else.

For the Raiders, it was another troubling reminder that their defensive shortcomings aren’t merely statistical anomalies. They are vulnerabilities opponents can identify on film, build game plans around and exploit.

Perhaps most discouraging was the predictability of it all.

The Raiders knew what was coming. Everyone knew what was coming.

Yet knowing and stopping are two entirely different propositions.

And on a Sunday when the Rams desperately needed to make a statement, they did so by attacking the Raiders right where they were most vulnerable.

Thirty-eight carries. 199 yards.

Sometimes football really is that simple.

And sometimes, that’s what makes it so demoralizing for the team getting pushed around.

Only for the drive to stall at the Rams 25.

Credit the Rams defense, which stood tall in their moments of truth.

They understood the assignment. A wounded team needing a win played with the urgency to seize its chances and the precision to maximize them.

The Raiders supplied the opposite.

And by the time the deficit reached 22 points, the difference between the teams required very little further explanation.

Rams carved up the Raiders weakness

There was no mystery about how Sean McVay and the Rams would attack the Raiders on Sunday.

Not with Las Vegas arriving at Allegiant Stadium sporting the NFL’s fifth-worst run defense. And certainly not with a Rams offense desperate to rediscover its physical identity and get its season back on track.

The blueprint was obvious. Pound the football, establish control at the line of scrimmage and force the Raiders to prove they could stop it.

The Rams hammered away for 199 rushing yards on 38 carries, averaging over five yards per attempt in a punishing display that exposed one of the Raiders’ biggest weaknesses.

It wasn’t necessarily complicated football. In fact, that was the beauty of it from the Rams’ perspective.

McVay identified a vulnerability, attacked it relentlessly and watched his offensive line impose its will on a Raiders defense that had few answers.

And the ramifications extended well beyond the rushing statistics.

By establishing the ground game, the Rams created favorable down-and-distance situations, kept the Raiders’ pass rush from teeing off on Matthew Stafford and opened opportunities for their passing attack.

It was complementary offensive football at its finest, with the running game serving as the foundation for everything else.

For the Raiders, it was another troubling reminder that their defensive shortcomings aren’t merely statistical anomalies. They are vulnerabilities opponents can identify on film, build game plans around and exploit.

Perhaps most discouraging was the predictability of it all.

The Raiders knew what was coming. Everyone knew what was coming.

Yet knowing and stopping are two entirely different propositions.

And on a Sunday when the Rams desperately needed to make a statement, they did so by attacking the Raiders right where they were most vulnerable.

Thirty-eight carries. 199 yards.

Sometimes football really is that simple.

And sometimes, that’s what makes it so demoralizing for the team getting pushed around.

news.originalContent:

The Dolphins hadn’t held a single lead this season.

Until they met the Jets defense.

The previously winless Dolphins entered Sunday averaging just 14.0 points per game — tied with the Titans for fewest in the NFL. But they toyed with the Jets defense — particularly during the first half — during Gang Green’s 28-25 loss at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

The Jets won the opening toss and deferred, but the Dolphins promptly ripped off a seven-play, 76-yard touchdown drive for their first lead of the season. After the Jets tied it, the Dolphins responded with a 14-play, 60-yard touchdown drive for their second lead of the season — one they never relinquished.

It helped them take a commanding 21-7 lead into halftime. The Dolphins hadn’t even reached 21 points in four of their first five full games.

“Obviously, you don’t want to spot a team 21 points in the first half,” Demario Davis said. “They did a great job of creating some really long drives. They made some good plays. Shoutout to them and the plays that they made. It wasn’t necessarily anything we did wrong on the plays, but they just found a way to make a play in those situations.”

The Jets defense was better in the second half, surrendering just one touchdown. That one touchdown, though, was an unacceptable breakdown that hurt any chance of a comeback.

They trailed 21-17 with under five minutes to go, needing a stop to get the ball back with a chance to take the lead. But Malik Willis completed a pass to a wide-open Caleb Douglas near the left sideline and Minkah Fitzpatrick — who had a chance to stop Douglas for a short gain — took a bad angle and completely whiffed on the tackle.

Douglas went untouched the rest of the way for a 63-yard touchdown that gave the Dolphins a 28-17 lead with 4:44 left.

“We were supposed to have someone in the flat,” Fitzpatrick said. “It was in the flat. But I gotta make a tackle. … We let them make too many explosive plays.”

The Jets defense had one more chance to save face after they cut the deficit to three with 3:24 left in the game. But the Jets gave up two first downs, allowing the Dolphins to run out the clock without the Jets offense getting another shot to either tie or win the game.

They seemed ill-prepared for Willis, who finished with 208 passing yards and two passing touchdowns along with 37 rushing yards and another touchdown on the ground. His scrambling ability helped the Dolphins extend drives, especially in the first half.

“He’s an athletic guy, he’s a talented guy,” Dane Belton said. “No matter what people say about him, as far as the start to this year, he’s had success in this league before. He’s very talented.

“We definitely want to get out to a better start, especially when you put the defense out first. We expect a little different result.”

The pressure is mounting on USC head coach Lincoln Riley, and the results aren’t meeting expectations.

After the Trojans suffered a devastating loss on the road to the Wisconsin Badgers on Saturday night, Keyshawn Johnson released a 2 two-minute, 42-second video of him calling USC a “F—ing joke.”

We really just lost to Wisconsin… Lincoln Riley I respect you but it just ain’t working out. Tough decisions have to be made USC. 🤷🏾‍♂️ #USC #FightOn pic.twitter.com/VlYOGlzvEZ

“Enough is enough,” Johnson said after calling out Riley and the Trojans.

Johnson opened up the video and said all he could do is “sit here and laugh.”

“We really just lost to Wisconsin. Not only did we lose, we got run out of the building,” Johnson said.

Johnson went on to call out the poor performance of the Trojans offense on Saturday after they scored one touchdown in the second quarter of a 24-7 loss to Wisconsin.

The Trojans offense finished the game throwing for 258 yards from quarterback Jayden Maiava, who completed 31 of 50 passes with two interceptions, while the USC offensive line gave up five sacks.

USC’s running game had its worst performance of the year, as they combined for -17 rushing yards, while running back King Miller ran the ball 11 times for eight yards.

Johnson said he was sick of what he was watching with USC and started to talk about how well UCLA — who just improved to 7-0 with wins against Oregon, Wisconsin, and Michigan State — under first-year head coach Bob Chesney.

He also congratulated Wisconsin’s head coach.

“Congratulations, Luke Fickell. Coach Fickell, you did an amazing job. You really did. You and your staff put it together,” Johnson said. “Hopefully you get one of these real Power-5 jobs. …Right now, maybe you could be our head coach.”

Johnson went on to say that he respects Riley and likes him, but thinks a divorce between him and the program is needed.

“We gotta recognize and understand that, and make some tough decisions,” Johnson said. “Sometimes tough decisions have got to be made. Whether you want to whether you don’t. They gotta be made.”

At the end of the video, Johnson went on to call for the USC financial boosters, administration, and “financial people” to make the tough decision on Riley.

If USC chooses to move on from Riley, they would be expected to buy him out at $70 million.

It feels like we go through this every year because … well, we go through this every year.

We go through stretches of the season when Mikal Bridges can’t buy a bucket and, worse, when he goes a string of games in a row when you have to check the final boxscore to make sure he’s played at all.

That last part, of course, is never in question because, when Bridges took the Garden floor Sunday night against the Magic, he extended his NBA games-played streak to 641. Bridges really does play every day. And there really should be no reason to remind you that he’s played quite well in a lot of them, including the 166 he’d played as a Knick ahead of the weekend.

It’s just that, when most pro basketball players go cold, they don’t take it to the wild extremes that Bridges does. When he goes into a funk, it sort of feels like he’s entered witness protection.

news.originalContent:

Jordyn Woods and Karl-Anthony Towns went all out and were completely unrecognizable in their “Game of Thrones”-inspired Halloween costumes.

The couple was snapped in New York City on Saturday in their jaw-dropping costumes. Woods went out in a White Walker look, while Towns dressed up as the Night King.

Towns, 30, carried a machete as a prop, while Woods, 29, also clearly spared no expense, rocking a blonde wig and contrasting sharply with her husband, who wore all black.

Both sported intricate, ghoulish makeup.

The two even went out to eat at a restaurant in their wild getups, sitting down at what appeared to be Sartiano’s in SoHo on Prince Street, according to The Post.

Both the New York Knicks star and the model are big “Game of Thrones” fans. In April, “Game of Thrones” star Kit Harington went to Game 1 of the Knicks playoff series against the Atlanta Hawks at Madison Square Garden and his interaction with Towns went viral.

Towns joked to Harington, “I would bend the knee, but my knee hurts right now,” referencing Harington’s character on the HBO hit, Jon Snow, memorably refusing to bend the knee to Emilia Clarke’s character, Daenerys Targaryen.

This year also marks Towns and Woods’ first Halloween as a married couple.

They tied the knot in August in a star-studded ceremony in Malibu, California. Celeb guests included Kylie Jenner and boyfriend Timothée Chalamet, Justin Bieber and wife Hailey Bieber, Jada Pinkett Smith, Teyana Taylor, Gayle King, and Michael B. Jordan, as well as Ben Stiller and wife Christine Taylor.

Woods was by her husband’s side earlier this month at the New York Knicks’ season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday at Madison Square Garden.

She debuted a new version of her now iconic lucky orange game-winning bag, sporting the Woods by Jordyn Tux Clutch Mini bag in the new color Trophy Gold.

The Knicks won the NBA championship in June.

The three-story building at 228 Manhattan Beach Boulevard, just blocks from the Pacific Ocean, is being offered through a competitive bidding process

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Footwear brand Skechers is putting its longtime Manhattan Beach headquarters on the market just eight years after an extensive renovation transformed the building into a purpose-built corporate home.

The three-story building at 228 Manhattan Beach Boulevard, just blocks from the Pacific Ocean, is being offered through a competitive bidding process handled by commercial real estate firm CBRE.

Spanning approximately 28,600 square feet, the property could be worth close to $100 million, although no official asking price has been disclosed.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Originally built in 1982, the headquarters underwent a major refurbishment in 2018, reinforcing its role as a dedicated base for the company. It features a private, three-level underground parking garage with 69 spaces, as well as the potential for ground-floor retail.

Now, the building is to be delivered vacant to its next owner, a striking turn for a property extensively upgraded less than a decade ago to accommodate the business.

Skechers has not disclosed the reasons behind the decision to sell the property, and it remains unclear whether employees will relocate to another office or what will happen to the company’s apparel store operating from the site.

The property occupies a prime position in downtown Manhattan Beach, within walking distance of the beach, Manhattan Beach Pier, restaurants and shops. Its location and size are likely to attract investors seeking a foothold in one of Southern California’s most desirable coastal markets.

CBRE vice chairman Stephen Somer said vacant office buildings of this scale and quality in downtown Manhattan Beach were exceptionally rare, highlighting the opportunity for a new owner to take immediate possession.

Real estate website Movoto estimates the property’s value at approximately $92.8 million, with a projected range of $83.5 million to $102 million.

The listing also comes as the South Bay office market navigates elevated vacancies. Regional office vacancy reached 23.6 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, according to a Colliers report, although average asking rents rose 3.5 per cent year-on-year.

Whether the headquarters will remain an office building or eventually be repurposed is also unknown, with no confirmed information establishing its redevelopment rights.

Incumbent President Iliana Iotova received between 35 and 36.5 percent of votes on Sunday, according to exit polls. She will now face former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, who scored between 31 and 33.5 percent, in a second round on November 1.

Minister of Interior Ivan Demerdzhiev said the elections “took place peacefully, without the usual practices of vote buying and vote manipulation”, Bulgarian National Television reported.

The NATO and European Union member state saw 27 presidential candidates run in the election.

A run-off was expected, as turnout must reach more than 50 percent of registered voters, and the candidate must secure more than 50 percent of the votes to win in the first round.

Voter turnout was 22.2 percent as of 8pm local time (18:00 GMT), according to the Measure polling agency.

Rising energy costs, inflation, attacks in the Black Sea and Russia’s war in Ukraine were the major issues in the lead-up to the vote.

A series of drone strikes on ships off Bulgaria’s coast, condemned by both candidates, dominated headlines during the campaign period.

Leftist Iotova is backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev, whose Progressive Bulgaria party enjoyed success in April’s parliamentary elections. Iotova became president in January after serving as vice president.

A former member of the European Parliament and a journalist, she ran as an independent with the backing of both Progressive Bulgaria and the Socialist Party.

Should she win, she is expected to keep Bulgaria in line with Europe, while calling for improved relations with Russia.

After casting her vote, Yotova said she wanted to address “the dire issue of poverty” in Bulgaria, as well as “inequalities and regional disputes”, the AFP news agency reported.

“I believe that there must be peace, stability, and security,” she added.

Gyurov has the support of the country’s pro-Western opposition and signed a security cooperation agreement with Ukraine as prime minister.

He said on Sunday that he wanted “a Bulgaria that looks forward, a country that is European, free, and proud”.

“Next week, Bulgaria must choose between two personalities, two directions,” he said after the vote, and invited Iotova to a debate before the next round.

Although the role of president is largely ceremonial, the president leads the armed forces, can veto legislation and sign treaties.

news.originalContent:
French superstar Kylian Mbappe scores a brace for Madrid to inflict Barcelona’s first domestic defeat of the campaign.

Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 El Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.

French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before half-time on Sunday, then slotted home late on to inflict Barca’s first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions.

Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick’s Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week.

The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday in the Champions League.

Barca won six of the seven previous Clasicos since the German arrived, but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho’s side.

“In general, we didn’t have a great game. In the first half, we weren’t ourselves; there were a lot of things we could have done better,” Barcelona midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

“We wanted to win the Clasico in front of our fans, but the season is very long… a league is not won here.”

Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions, and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho.

After two trophyless seasons, Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try to stop Barca’s dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track.

The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities.

Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking to Lamine Yamal’s shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger.

Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, back-heeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened.

The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark.

Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead.

Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca’s Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net.

Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser, but teenage sensation Yamal, for once, miscued in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level.

The game opened up, and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid’s lead before half-time, drilling into the side netting.

Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe.

Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark.

Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga’s top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham’s legs, and Lunin could not keep the shot out.

The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin a corner as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails.

Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch, and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen.

There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans, though, as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal.

Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net, with Joan Garcia drawn out of position.

news.originalContent:
National Rally’s Le Pen launches presidential campaign against the backdrop of mass protests and social and economic discontent.

Orleans, France – Marine Le Pen took to the stage with a clear message: She would lead France’s “renaissance” as the country sank into crisis – and she would do so soon.

The far-right figure’s words were met with cheers from thousands of supporters gathered in Orleans in central France on Sunday, as she launched her presidential campaign against a backdrop of mass demonstrations and widespread social and economic discontent.

“Marine présidente!” the crowd chanted, waving French flags beneath a sea of red and blue lights. Organisers said 8,500 supporters had gathered in a venue transformed into a fort for the event.

Standing tall on stage in a pink blazer, her hair impeccably coiffed, Le Pen spoke with the confidence of a leader who believes the presidency is within reach.

Riding high in the polls, with candidates from the right, left and centre trailing behind her, she presented the election as a historic opportunity to restore France’s past glory.

“This is a story to be written, a destiny to be fulfilled,” she told the crowd, which erupted in cheers.

Her pitch was a promise to restore authority and security in a country she portrayed as having lost control.

“We are going to re-establish the rule of law,” she said, drawing loud applause from supporters wearing “Marine présidente” T-shirts.

Manon Funeau, 21, a business school student, was among the supporters.

“What they propose are values that resonate with me, that vibrate within me,” she said. “Honestly, I feel at home here.”

Le Pen’s speech comes as the country is at a crossroads. France has been shaken by a wave of protests since mid-September, a movement sparked by high school students in a Paris suburb that grew into a nationwide mobilisation tapping into widespread discontent.

Over the past two weekends, largely peaceful protests have been accompanied by episodes of violence on a scale rarely seen in recent years.

On October 17, shops were looted and ransacked, and more than 2,000 people were arrested as hundreds of thousands took to the streets of French cities. A similar dynamic unfolded the following weekend, though on a smaller scale. The protests show little sign of abating, with calls for further demonstrations already circulating.

The unrest has given Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) an opportunity to play one of its favourite cards: presenting itself as the guarantor of law and order. It has fuelled criticism of President Emmanuel Macron over his handling of public security, allowing Le Pen to accuse him of incompetence and the far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon – a contender in the coming elections – of encouraging the violence.

“I believe that my country is currently drifting off course,” said Nadede, a 56-year-old who began voting for RN in 2024 over what she said was the country’s growing lack of security. She did not spell out any specific event.

“I think that the only person capable of setting it back on the right track is Marine Le Pen – especially since, up until now, everyone else who has run for office has struggled to do so,” she said.

Outside the convention hall, the scale of the security operation offered a glimpse of the tensions surrounding the event. Police checks began at departure stations in Paris and continued on arrival, while officers in full gear moved through train carriages during the journey.

Orleans itself had been brought to a near standstill. All businesses were shut and public transport suspended.

Standing almost alone in the city’s main square was the statue of Joan of Arc, surrounded only by fences. A day earlier, about 3,000 police officers had been deployed to prevent unrest as anti-RN protesters gathered against what they say is a xenophobic and racist party.

Orleans was no casual choice. For a party that has long sought to cast itself as the guardian of French identity and national sovereignty, the city is inseparable from the story of Joan of Arc, the 15th-century heroine who helped lift the English siege of Orléans in 1429 and became a symbol of France’s resistance and liberation.

For decades, the far right has claimed her as an emblem of national pride, invoking the image of a warrior who came to save France from foreign domination. Le Pen herself has drawn parallels between Joan’s mission and her political ambitions.

The crowd at the RN Congress offered a glimpse of how the party has expanded its appeal to a wider section of society: from young people from urban centres to middle-class workers who used to vote for the centrist party.

Only a few years ago, the party was still considered on the fringes of French politics. Its growth has been driven in part by a carefully crafted strategy known as dédiabolisation, or de-demonisation, developed over the past two decades to broaden the party’s base while tempering its rhetoric and distancing it from positions that had made it toxic to many voters.

The party has long been associated with racism, xenophobia and anti-Semitism. Le Pen’s father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, was convicted of hate speech, including for describing Nazi gas chambers as “a detail of history”. He was expelled from the party in 2015.

Marine Le Pen has sought to broaden RN’s appeal, combining restrictive immigration policies with promises of social protection. The party has gained ground in working-class areas traditionally associated with the left, including former Communist strongholds, by presenting itself as a defender of public services and the purchasing power of everyday people.

While RN has long abandoned some of its most radical proposals, including leaving the Eurozone and pursuing a fully fledged “Frexit”, the election of such a eurosceptic to the helm of the European Union’s second-largest economy would send shockwaves. She has pledged a referendum to challenge the primacy of EU law over migration policy, as well as an annual 11-billion-euro ($12.3bn) reduction in France’s contribution to the bloc.

The party’s membership has nearly tripled, with approximately 112,000 members now paying their dues, up from fewer than 37,000 in 2022.

“The party has been gaining ground at every level: mayors, deputies, senators. Usually, when a movement seems on the rise, people join,” said Baptiste Roger-Lacan, a historian and political analyst with a focus on far-right parties in Europe. “It also shows how it is less and less socially damaging to be a member of the RN.”

But the party’s programme “is still fraught with fiscal absurdity”, Roger-Lacan said. “They still want to implement racist laws, which are bound to provoke widespread anger, and their diplomatic agenda is still pro-Russian and anti-EU – even if they don’t advocate Frexit any more.”

Jordan Bardella, Le Pen’s second-in-command and Le Pen protégé – an impeccably dressed 31-year-old who looks like a cross between the Wolf of Wall Street and Superman’s alter ego, Clark Kent – also spoke at the event.

“No one should be intimidated by their political opinions,” he said, speaking ahead of his mentor.

Some observers say the October 17 protests and their aftermath have proved a gift to RN, allowing the party to not only reinforce its law-and-order message but also to shift attention away from recent difficulties.

In September, investigative outlet Mediapart published allegations that Bardella had expressed anti-Semitic views in private messages dating back to his teenage years. He denied the allegations and announced legal action against the journalists.

The episode posed a challenge for a party that has spent years trying to shed its xenophobic image and recast itself as a supporter of Israel.

Bardella has also reportedly differed with Le Pen over the party’s economic agenda and whether to make her proposed ban on the wearing of the Islamic headscarf in public spaces a central campaign issue.

Yet, at the Congress, those tensions appeared to have been set aside, at least publicly.

“Marine president – a Bardella government” was the slogan, projecting unity as Le Pen launched her presidential bid and Bardella positioned himself as her prospective head of government.

news.originalContent:
The Department of Justice has faced criticism that its lawsuit is aimed at blocking a Democratic victory in a key race.

United States Attorney General Todd Blanche has defended the Department of Justice’s decision to sue to prevent the certification of a Republican loss in Alaska’s tight Senate race.

On Sunday, Blanche did a tour of the morning political shows in the US, making stops at CNN’s State of the Union TV programme and CBS’s Face the Nation.

In each appearance, he faced pointed questions about the legality of the Justice Department’s efforts, responding, in some cases, with open frustration.

“ Why is this controversial?” Blanche asked CNN host Dana Bash at one point. He proceeded to accuse one of the candidates in the Senate race of intentionally trying to confuse voters.

“We’re going to try to create a situation where that can be remedied,” he said. “That shouldn’t be something that is causing this shock and horror.”

But the Justice Department’s lawsuit, filed on October 22, has been the subject of bipartisan criticism.

Many have accused the administration of President Donald Trump of laying the groundwork to block a Democratic win in the race. Trump himself claimed to have authorised the lawsuit.

“I’m the one who said do it,” he told reporters on Friday.

During the midterm elections on November 3, citizens in Alaska will vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country, which will help decide whether Republicans maintain their majority in the chamber.

Senator Dan S Sullivan, the Republican incumbent, is seeking to defend his seat in the US Senate. But he faces fierce competition from former US Representative Mary Peltola, a Democrat.

Also in the running is another candidate named Dan J Sullivan, a former Forest Service employee.

The second Sullivan’s decision to run has raised concerns that he is a spoiler candidate, whose presence on the ballot is designed to draw votes away from the incumbent.

But the Forest Service worker has denied any such intent. Such allegations, he said, are “entirely false”.

“I am not a registered Democrat, and I have had no conversations whatsoever with the Peltola campaign about my candidacy,” the second Sullivan wrote in a letter to Alaska’s lieutenant governor before the state’s primaries.

“I have considered running for political office for over a decade. I made the decision to formally run for the United States Senate in the upcoming primary election because Senator Sullivan has routinely failed the people of Alaska, and they deserve a better representative. It is my right to do so.”

Four candidates advanced to the final round of voting after Alaska’s August primaries. They included Peltola and both Sullivans. The two men are running as Republicans.

The Justice Department has argued that its lawsuit – filed less than two weeks before the midterm elections – is necessary “to protect the integrity” of the election.

Any result in the Senate race, it argues, would be “tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J Sullivan”.

The department has therefore called on the US District Court in Alaska to issue an order declaring the race’s certification “unlawful” and barring the state from “allowing such a certification to occur”.

Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections, though Congress has the right to pass regulations concerning federal votes.

It is highly unusual for a presidential administration to inject itself into issues of state election certification, and experts say such a move is likely to be deemed illegal.

Already, in June, Alaska’s Supreme Court ruled that both Sullivans could compete in the Senate race. The state’s Division of Elections has also taken steps to reduce voter confusion.

The November 3 ballot, for instance, will list Dan S Sullivan as the incumbent and as a “registered Republican”.

Dan J Sullivan, meanwhile, will have the suffix “Jr” added to his name, and his party affiliation will be left blank, despite the candidate identifying as Republican.

But in Sunday’s television appearances, Blanche — who leads the Department of Justice and formerly served as Trump’s personal lawyer — argued that merely having two Sullivans on the ballot is a recipe for confusion.

“It is wrong,” Blanche told CNN. “Putting aside whether we’re going to win or lose in the courts, putting aside what the Alaskan Supreme Court has done, in our system, we should not have a candidate who has to worry about another candidate being on the ballot for no other reason than to confuse voters.”

Blanche also denied any impropriety in Trump saying he ordered the lawsuit.

“He’s supposed to make sure that everything in this country is running right, including elections,” Blanche said.

Historically, the Justice Department has embraced a norm of judicial independence, though critics have accused the Trump administration of wielding its prosecutorial powers for political gain.

Bash, the CNN host, raised some of those concerns, pointing to Trump’s comments accusing Democrats of cheating, as well as his history of election denialism.

The president has long denied his loss in the 2020 presidential race, and his supporters sought to block the certification of that election, notably by storming the US Capitol on January 6, 2021.

When Bash pointed to that incident, Blanche chided her: “Oh, you’ve got to stop it with that.”

“Why are you yelling at me?” Bash responded as the two talked over each other.

“You are not being a real person. Come on, man,” Blanche continued. “That is crazy.”

He also denied that Trump was setting the stage for a contested election if the Democrat Peltola were to win. Instead, he framed the lawsuit as setting the stage for further investigations into any eventual results.

“The relief that we’re seeking – which, again, isn’t to determine who the senator is, it’s not to try to overturn something the state is going to do – it’s just to make sure that the ballots that come in are kept in a way that may allow a court to investigate further,” Blanche said.

Speaking to CBS, Blanche also dodged a question about whether Trump personally asked him to file the lawsuit.

“I will never, ever, ever talk about communications that I have with the president of the United States. I never have, and I never will,” Blanche said.

The race to control the US Senate is expected to be a nail-biter, with Republicans holding a slim majority at present: They have 53 seats in the 100-member chamber.

Only a third of the Senate’s seats – 35 in total – will be up for grabs in the midterm races, as terms in the chamber last six years and are staggered across different election years.

Trump’s Republican Party is projected to face an uphill battle to protect its congressional majorities, amid backlash against the rising cost of living and Trump’s own withering poll numbers.

Roughly seven Senate elections are considered toss-ups, including the Alaska race.

In early October, The New York Times and Siena College released a poll finding Peltola leading the incumbent Sullivan by nearly 7 percentage points, one of the widest margins of any of the toss-up states.

news.originalTitle: ماسک می‌گوید استارلینک را برای اوکراین محدود کرد چون برای عملیات هجومی استفاده می‌شد
news.title: ماسک می‌گوید استارلینک را برای اوکراین محدود کرد چون برای عملیات هجومی استفاده می‌شد
news.originalSummary:
ایلان ماسک می‌گوید که اسپیس‌ایکس خدمات اینترنت استارلینک در اوکراین را محدود کرده است، در حالی‌که مقامات اوکراین گفته بودند محدودیت در اتصال به این سامانه اینترنت ماهواره‌ای برطرف شده‌ است.

آقای ماسک اوکراین را به نقض شروط استفاده از استارلینک و به کار گرفتن آن برای عملیات نظامی متهم کرد؛ او اما مشکل مشابهی را که همزمان در دسترسی ارتش اوکراین به استارشیلد پیش آمد منتسب به شرکتش ندانست. استارشیلد

news.originalContent:
ایلان ماسک می‌گوید که اسپیس‌ایکس خدمات اینترنت استارلینک در اوکراین را محدود کرده است، در حالی‌که مقامات اوکراین گفته بودند محدودیت در اتصال به این سامانه اینترنت ماهواره‌ای برطرف شده‌ است.

آقای ماسک اوکراین را به نقض شروط استفاده از استارلینک و به کار گرفتن آن برای عملیات نظامی متهم کرد؛ او اما مشکل مشابهی را که همزمان در دسترسی ارتش اوکراین به استارشیلد پیش آمد منتسب به شرکتش ندانست. استارشیلد نسخه نظامی استارلینک است و در مدیریت دولت و ارتش آمریکاست.

کی‌یف تاکنون رسما واکنشی نشان نداده است اما سرگئی بسکرستنو، مشاور رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، گفت که حرف او «بسیار عجیب» است.

آقای ماسک پیش‌تر اختلال عمدی در محدودیت اتصال به استارلینک را رد کرده بود، درحالی‌که اوکراین گفته بود بیش از یک هفته عملیات دفاعی‌اش مختل شده است.

این مسئله نخستین بار هفته گذشته در میانه اختلاف نظر واشنگتن و کی‌یف بر سر حمله به زیرساخت‌های نفتی روسیه مطرح شد.

پس از آن، دونالد ترامپ گفت که از مالک تسلا و ایکس خواسته است که ارتباط را برقرار کند، درحالی‌که بارها گفته است که او از آقای ماسک نخواسته بود که این سرویس را محدود کند.

آقای ماسک روز شنبه در ایکس نوشت: «استفاده از استارلینک، یک سرویس تجاری غیرنظامی، برای هجوم پهپادی با هدف کشتن مردم، هرگز مجاز نبوده است و نباید هم باشد.»

او نوشت: «ارتش اوکراین شروط استفاده از استارلینک را نقض کرد و از آن برای هجوم پهپادی با هدف کشتن مردم استفاده کرد. آن راه گریز هفته گذشته بسته شد.»

او نوشت که اسپیس‌ایکس «بیش از هر شرکت خصوصی دیگری در کره زمین» در دفاع از اوکراین کوشیده است اما تاکید کرد که استارشلید سامانه‌ای متفاوت و در کنترل دولت ایالات متحده است: «اینکه تصمیم بگیرند چه کاری کنند، به خودشان مربوط است.»

او در پستی دیگر نوشت: «[استارلینک] می‌تواند برای زیرساخت‌های نظامی به کار گرفته شود اما نمی‌تواند برای حملاتی استفاده شود که آشکارا تهاجمی‌ هستند که استارلینک را به هدفی مشروع برای حمله متقابل بدل می‌کنند.»

آقای بسکرستنو در واکنش به این اظهارات در تلگرام نوشت که پایانه‌های استارلینک فعال در اوکراین در عمق خاک روسیه کار نمی‌کنند: «بنابراین، ما نمی‌توانیم از استارلینک تجاری برای حملات دوربرد و میانبرد استفاده کنیم.»

او  نوشت که «بسیار عجیب است که ایلان ماسک از محدودیت‌های استارلینک در اوکراین آگاه نیست.»

وزارت دفاع اوکراین اظهارنظری نکرده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اوکراین هم از سرویس غیرنظامی استارلینک و هم از استارشلید امن‌تر استفاده می‌کند. هر دوی این سامانه‌ها بر شبکه‌هایی از ماهواره‌های مدار پایین زمین متکی هستند که اسپیس‌ایکس به فضا پرتاب کرده است.

استارلینک به یگان‌های نظامی امکان هماهنگی می‌دهد، به‌ویژه در مناطق دورافتاده میدان نبرد، در حالی‌که استارشلید به اپراتورهای پهپاد اوکراین اجازه می‌دهد اهداف را بی‌درنگ مشاهده کنند و پهپادهای رهگیر را هدایت کنند.

روسیه به استارلینک دسترسی ندارد بنابراین هنگامی که اوکراین موشک‌ یا پهپاد دوربرد را برای هدف قرار دادن پالایشگاه‌های نفت به عمق خاک روسیه می‌فرستد، این شبکه کار نمی‌کند.

وزیر دفاع اوکراین دیروز گفته بود که اتصال «پایدار»  شده است و پهپادها می‌توانند به سرعت‌هایی بیش از ۴۰۰ کیلومتر در ساعت (۲۴۹ مایل در ساعت) برسند. کی‌یف پیش‌تر گفته بود که ارتباط پهپادها در سرعت‌های بالاتر از ۱۶۱ کیلومتر در ساعت قطع می‌شود.

ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، هم در تلگرام نوشت سرعت‌ اکنون همان است «که باید باشد.»

آقای ماسک توضیح نداد که چرا اسپیس‌ایکس هفته گذشته تصمیم گرفت تغییراتی در سرویس خود ایجاد کند، در حالی‌که استفاده گسترده اوکراین از استارلینک چند سال است که ادامه دارد.

مشکل ارتباط با استارلینک همزمان با بن‌بست دیپلماتیک پرتنش ولودیمیر زلنسکی و دونالد ترامپ بر سر حمله به زیرساخت‌های نفتی روسیه رخ داد.

آقای ترامپ می‌گوید که حمله به پالایشگاه‌های نفت روسیه قیمت جهانی را افزایش داده است. اوکراین می‌گوید منابع مالی ارتش روسیه را محدود می‌کند.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا که انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای را عین نارضایتی داخلی از افزایش قیمت سوخت پیش رو دارد، برخی تحریم‌های روسیه را لغو کرد و با مسکو به توافق رسید که گازوئیل را به بازار ایالات متحده و بازار جهانی عرضه کند. این تصمیم با انتقاد شدید متحدان اروپایی مواجه شد.

آقای زلنسکی در ابتدا موافقت کرده بود که به شرط توقف حملات روسیه به زیرساخت‌هایش چنین کند؛ او اما پس از چند بار بی‌اعتنایی مسکو به این شرط، حملات را از سر گرفت.

رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین گفت که ایالات متحده، علاوه بر محدود کردن استارلینک در اوکراین، تهدید کرده بود که در صورت متوقف نشدن حملات، اشتراک‌ اطلاعاتی را نیز قطع خواهد کرد. آقای ترامپ این موضوع را تکذیب کرده است.

ایلان ماسک می‌گوید که اسپیس‌ایکس خدمات اینترنت استارلینک در اوکراین را محدود کرده است، در حالی‌که مقامات اوکراین گفته بودند محدودیت در اتصال به این سامانه اینترنت ماهواره‌ای برطرف شده‌ است.

آقای ماسک اوکراین را به نقض شروط استفاده از استارلینک و به کار گرفتن آن برای عملیات نظامی متهم کرد؛ او اما مشکل مشابهی را که همزمان در دسترسی ارتش اوکراین به استارشیلد پیش آمد منتسب به شرکتش ندانست. استارشیلد نسخه نظامی استارلینک است و در مدیریت دولت و ارتش آمریکاست.

کی‌یف تاکنون رسما واکنشی نشان نداده است اما سرگئی بسکرستنو، مشاور رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، گفت که حرف او «بسیار عجیب» است.

آقای ماسک پیش‌تر اختلال عمدی در محدودیت اتصال به استارلینک را رد کرده بود، درحالی‌که اوکراین گفته بود بیش از یک هفته عملیات دفاعی‌اش مختل شده است.

این مسئله نخستین بار هفته گذشته در میانه اختلاف نظر واشنگتن و کی‌یف بر سر حمله به زیرساخت‌های نفتی روسیه مطرح شد.

پس از آن، دونالد ترامپ گفت که از مالک تسلا و ایکس خواسته است که ارتباط را برقرار کند، درحالی‌که بارها گفته است که او از آقای ماسک نخواسته بود که این سرویس را محدود کند.

آقای ماسک روز شنبه در ایکس نوشت: «استفاده از استارلینک، یک سرویس تجاری غیرنظامی، برای هجوم پهپادی با هدف کشتن مردم، هرگز مجاز نبوده است و نباید هم باشد.»

او نوشت: «ارتش اوکراین شروط استفاده از استارلینک را نقض کرد و از آن برای هجوم پهپادی با هدف کشتن مردم استفاده کرد. آن راه گریز هفته گذشته بسته شد.»

او نوشت که اسپیس‌ایکس «بیش از هر شرکت خصوصی دیگری در کره زمین» در دفاع از اوکراین کوشیده است اما تاکید کرد که استارشلید سامانه‌ای متفاوت و در کنترل دولت ایالات متحده است: «اینکه تصمیم بگیرند چه کاری کنند، به خودشان مربوط است.»

او در پستی دیگر نوشت: «[استارلینک] می‌تواند برای زیرساخت‌های نظامی به کار گرفته شود اما نمی‌تواند برای حملاتی استفاده شود که آشکارا تهاجمی‌ هستند که استارلینک را به هدفی مشروع برای حمله متقابل بدل می‌کنند.»

آقای بسکرستنو در واکنش به این اظهارات در تلگرام نوشت که پایانه‌های استارلینک فعال در اوکراین در عمق خاک روسیه کار نمی‌کنند: «بنابراین، ما نمی‌توانیم از استارلینک تجاری برای حملات دوربرد و میانبرد استفاده کنیم.»

او  نوشت که «بسیار عجیب است که ایلان ماسک از محدودیت‌های استارلینک در اوکراین آگاه نیست.»

وزارت دفاع اوکراین اظهارنظری نکرده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اوکراین هم از سرویس غیرنظامی استارلینک و هم از استارشلید امن‌تر استفاده می‌کند. هر دوی این سامانه‌ها بر شبکه‌هایی از ماهواره‌های مدار پایین زمین متکی هستند که اسپیس‌ایکس به فضا پرتاب کرده است.

استارلینک به یگان‌های نظامی امکان هماهنگی می‌دهد، به‌ویژه در مناطق دورافتاده میدان نبرد، در حالی‌که استارشلید به اپراتورهای پهپاد اوکراین اجازه می‌دهد اهداف را بی‌درنگ مشاهده کنند و پهپادهای رهگیر را هدایت کنند.

روسیه به استارلینک دسترسی ندارد بنابراین هنگامی که اوکراین موشک‌ یا پهپاد دوربرد را برای هدف قرار دادن پالایشگاه‌های نفت به عمق خاک روسیه می‌فرستد، این شبکه کار نمی‌کند.

وزیر دفاع اوکراین دیروز گفته بود که اتصال «پایدار»  شده است و پهپادها می‌توانند به سرعت‌هایی بیش از ۴۰۰ کیلومتر در ساعت (۲۴۹ مایل در ساعت) برسند. کی‌یف پیش‌تر گفته بود که ارتباط پهپادها در سرعت‌های بالاتر از ۱۶۱ کیلومتر در ساعت قطع می‌شود.

ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، هم در تلگرام نوشت سرعت‌ اکنون همان است «که باید باشد.»

آقای ماسک توضیح نداد که چرا اسپیس‌ایکس هفته گذشته تصمیم گرفت تغییراتی در سرویس خود ایجاد کند، در حالی‌که استفاده گسترده اوکراین از استارلینک چند سال است که ادامه دارد.

مشکل ارتباط با استارلینک همزمان با بن‌بست دیپلماتیک پرتنش ولودیمیر زلنسکی و دونالد ترامپ بر سر حمله به زیرساخت‌های نفتی روسیه رخ داد.

آقای ترامپ می‌گوید که حمله به پالایشگاه‌های نفت روسیه قیمت جهانی را افزایش داده است. اوکراین می‌گوید منابع مالی ارتش روسیه را محدود می‌کند.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا که انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای را عین نارضایتی داخلی از افزایش قیمت سوخت پیش رو دارد، برخی تحریم‌های روسیه را لغو کرد و با مسکو به توافق رسید که گازوئیل را به بازار ایالات متحده و بازار جهانی عرضه کند. این تصمیم با انتقاد شدید متحدان اروپایی مواجه شد.

آقای زلنسکی در ابتدا موافقت کرده بود که به شرط توقف حملات روسیه به زیرساخت‌هایش چنین کند؛ او اما پس از چند بار بی‌اعتنایی مسکو به این شرط، حملات را از سر گرفت.

رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین گفت که ایالات متحده، علاوه بر محدود کردن استارلینک در اوکراین، تهدید کرده بود که در صورت متوقف نشدن حملات، اشتراک‌ اطلاعاتی را نیز قطع خواهد کرد. آقای ترامپ این موضوع را تکذیب کرده است.
